summary:
CHRONOS // SPHEREx (chronosspherex.earth) is an interactive, browser-based time-domain infrared sky observatory built to accelerate the discovery of Planet X, cold brown dwarfs (Y/T/L dwarfs), and variable stars in NASA SPHEREx mission data (0.75–5.00 μm).

Inspired by WiseView and tailored for SPHEREx’s 6 Linear Variable Filter detector arrays and 102 spectral channels, the platform lets scientists and citizen astronomers enter any sky coordinates, blink multi-epoch 2025–2026 NASA IRSA passes, compare epochs with an interactive split-curtain divider and 3.5x centroid loupe, isolate moving objects via Dipole Difference Imaging, and inspect WCS North-Up reprojected NASA Level-2 FITS cutouts. Clicking any star or pixel extracts an on-the-fly 102-band near-infrared spectrum anchored to real ESA Gaia DR3, 2MASS, and NASA AllWISE photometry (mJy), alongside multi-epoch light curves. The system is verified end-to-end across all five benchmark targets—Barnard’s Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi Ba+Bb, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis—propagated to exact 2025–2026 astrometric epochs.
details:
Live Observatory: https://chronosspherex.earth

Public Repository: https://github.com/mekamim/chronos-spherex

What It Does & How It Works

CHRONOS // SPHEREx unifies multi-epoch astrometric blinking and 102-channel infrared spectrophotometry (0.75–5.00 μm) in a single browser-based instrument:

• Universal Sky Search & Astrometric Epoch Propagation: Users enter coordinates (decimal degrees or HMS/DMS) or object names (e.g., M31, Wolf 359, TRAPPIST-1, Barnard's Star). High-proper-motion targets are propagated in 3D via Astropy SkyCoord.apply_space_motion() from catalog reference epochs (J2000.0 / WISE 2010.5) to exact 2025–2026 SPHEREx observation epochs (e.g., shifting Barnard's Star +266.5" North so it stays centered in 2025–2026 FITS cutouts).

• Multi-Epoch Blinker & 6 Inspection Modes: Supports Ping-Pong, WiseView A/B Blink, and Time-Lapse playback across observed NASA IRSA SIAv2 orbital passes (clustered with a 3.5-day step-stare gap), alongside an interactive Split-Curtain Epoch Comparator with a 3.5x centroid loupe, Dipole Difference Imaging (Epoch N − Epoch 1), Temporal Co-Add (Σ Epochs) for faint-object SNR boosting, False-Color Thermal RGB (D6/D4/D1), and native 6.15"/px NASA Level-2 Raw FITS inspection.

• On-the-Fly 102-Channel Spectrophotometer: Clicking any star or sky pixel extracts its 0.75–5.00 μm spectrum with molecular markers (H₂O, CH₄, CO, CO₂, PAH, H I) anchored to cataloged 2MASS (J, H, Ks) and WISE (W1, W2) flux densities (mJy), plus multi-epoch light curves.

• Calibrations & Exports: Includes Zodiacal Light (ZODI) subtraction toggling, HDU 2 32-bit FLAGS bitmask decoding, ESA Gaia DR3 proper motion overlays, cross-mission links (IRSA, CSA NEOSSat, SIMBAD, WiseView), and standard Multi-Extension FITS (.fits) exports with full RA---TAN / DEC--TAN WCS headers.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Discovering Planet X or free-floating Y-dwarfs (such as 250 K WISE 0855, undetectable in optical Gaia and SPHEREx D1–D3 while emerging at ~0.48 mJy in D6 when co-added) traditionally requires stitching together separate catalog queries, DS9/Python notebooks, and static viewers. CHRONOS // SPHEREx lowers the barrier so citizen scientists, students, and researchers can visually discover moving anomalies and inspect spectra in seconds directly at https://chronosspherex.earth.

Tools, Languages & Architecture

• Backend: Python, FastAPI, Uvicorn, Astropy (WCS, coordinates, FITS), SciPy, NumPy, Requests.

• Frontend: HTML5 Canvas (client-side asinh/linear/log stretching, Inferno/Viridis/Magma/Inverted colormaps), Vanilla JavaScript, CSS.

• Live Data APIs: NASA/IPAC IRSA SIAv2, IRSA IBE Level-2 FITS cutouts, and IRSA Gator (gaia_dr3_source & allwise_p3as_psd).

• Deployment & Open-Source Code (MIT License): Containerized with Docker for Google Cloud Run custom-domain hosting (chronosspherex.earth); public repository at https://github.com/mekamim/chronos-spherex

Creativity & Scientific Factors Considered

• Detector Roll Reprojection: Native SPHEREx Level-2 FITS cutouts arrive at arbitrary spacecraft roll angles (~ -178.9°); our engine reprojects them onto a North-Up, East-Left TAN WCS grid using Astropy WCS and bilinear/nearest-neighbor resampling.

• Data Transparency (RAW_FITS vs. MODEL_CUBE): Because individual SPHEREx passes cover one LVF strip at a time, MODEL_CUBE provides continuous 6-band/102-channel forward modeling calibrated to real 2MASS/WISE fluxes, while RAW_FITS displays un-modeled NASA detector pixels.

• Verification Across All 5 Benchmark Targets: Validated end-to-end on Barnard's Star, WISE 0855−0714, Epsilon Indi Ba+Bb, RW Aurigae, and R Draconis.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure

SI coding assistants (conversational LLMs) were utilized during development to accelerate FastAPI route scaffolding, HTML5 Canvas UI implementation, and automated verification scripts. All astrophysical formulas, 3D proper-motion epoch propagations, WCS transformations, IRSA catalog queries, and validation tests were reviewed, verified, and grounded against official NASA/IPAC IRSA and Astropy standards by the team.
